title: Maya / The AI-News Decoder — prompt pack
caption:
Every week, 40+ AI releases. Maybe 5 of them actually change how you build. The other 35 are funding rounds, founder drama, and demos that never ship.

I got tired of the FOMO, so I built a system: every morning I run the whole AI feed through Claude, and 15 minutes later I have a brief of what actually matters.

Here are the 5 prompts that run it — they're all on the slides, swipe through:

1. SOURCE & TRIAGE — kill the noise
2. WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED — strip the marketing
3. SIGNAL VS. THEATER — spot the hype
4. THE FRIDAY TEST — turn it into a decision
5. THE WEEKLY BRIEF — package it in 200 words

Comment SYSTEM and I'll DM you the full prompt system — copy-paste ready — plus the field guide it's built on.

— maya

promptParagraphs: Sort them into flagship releases, real capability shifts, and noise. Drop anything that's funding, drama, or a demo that hasn't shipped.
Return the 5 a working builder would regret missing — ranked, one line each.
Strip the marketing. Tell me what's usable today, what's a preview, and what's just a roadmap promise.
Then, in one sentence: what changes for someone building with this on Monday?
What did the demo quietly skip? What got the keynote clip but isn't shipping? What's a projection dressed up as a feature?
List every red flag. Shortest version possible.
Given all of the above, answer one question.
Can I use this on real work by Friday — yes or no?
If yes: the 3-step path to try it. If no: the one signal to watch that would change the answer.
Take the 5 releases I kept this week and the notes above.
Write a 200-word brief I can read in 90 seconds: what shipped, the line that matters, who should care, what to do this week.
Plain and concrete. No adjective I can't measure.
